### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**20** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3806b2e46a56c3537111fe8113d496b38ebaed9f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b5d06bec504a05306ae8c134fda7c59710484ab3` — the merge of head `4c2a96e4634eff78ff10613fec02d8c4a57543ce` into base `3806b2e46a56c3537111fe8113d496b38ebaed9f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b5d06bec504a05306ae8c134fda7c59710484ab3 && git checkout b5d06bec504a05306ae8c134fda7c59710484ab3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3806b2e46a56c3537111fe8113d496b38ebaed9f 4c2a96e4634eff78ff10613fec02d8c4a57543ce && git checkout -B drift-repro 3806b2e46a56c3537111fe8113d496b38ebaed9f && git merge --no-ff 4c2a96e4634eff78ff10613fec02d8c4a57543ce

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3806b2e46a56c3537111fe8113d496b38ebaed9f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4c2a96e4634eff78ff10613fec02d8c4a57543ce`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/comments.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/webhooks.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/attachments.ts

First round. Read: card #37610 (body, triage 7197373477, claim 7197524494), this PR's body, its nine-file list, the net diff against the merge-base `b1c41e55e2` (`main` has since touched none of the five scoped files), and the 69 check-runs on the head. Every check-run is completed, `success` or `skipped`, none red: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all read `success`.

The rest of the diff (the changeset and the three test files) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Catalog key set: right, an enlargement.** `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` goes from 44 to 50 keys in each of `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES`. Added in all four: `own_door_service_unregistered_plural`, `own_door_member_missing_plural`, `comment_doors_service_unregistered`, `comment_doors_member_missing`, `webhook_redeliver_service_unregistered`, `webhook_redeliver_member_missing`. No key is removed and no `en` value of an existing key moves.
- **Catalog values: one existing value moves, and it is declared.** `es-ES` `own_door_attachment_mutate` goes from singular to plural. Its only reader is the attachment bridge, which now pairs it with the plural sentences.
- **Each new key is closed the way the existing rows are.** The `_plural` pair takes exactly the placeholders of its singular twin in every locale (door, slot, producer; door, slot, member); the four whole sentences take none, and their callers pass none. Slot, member and package identifiers are left untranslated in all four locales.
- **Comment doors and redelivery door, wire: right.** Status `501`, code `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and the absence of `userMessage` are untouched. The four `en` values are byte-identical to the literals the two handlers held on the merge-base (each occurs once in the head catalog). A request whose top `Accept-Language` tag resolves to `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` or `es-ES` now reads that locale; no header, or a tag the catalog lacks, reads English.
- **Bridge doors, wire: right.** Print and personal-view leave `nounPlural` unset, so they read the same two keys with the same caller object as before: identical in every locale. Attachments: `en` moves "is" to "are", `es-ES` moves to a plural noun and verb, `zh-CN` and `ja-JP` are identical (their plural pair equals the singular pair byte for byte). The `es-ES` move goes past the card's letter, which names English only, but it is on the door the card names and the changeset states it.
- **Runtime types: not a published change.** `OwnDoorBridge.nounKey` becomes required, `nounPlural` is added and `requestLocaleOf` is exported from its module. `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` re-exports nothing from `domains/own-door-bridge.ts`, and the package `exports` map offers `.` and `./compiled-plugin-manifest-file` only, so no published accept set narrows.
- No spec export is added, removed or renamed, and no schema key is touched.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/runtime` patch match what the diff publishes: a catalog enlargement with no protocol kind, and a fix in a released package. `Check Changeset` is `success`.

Both declarations hold. The PR body and the changeset carry the same `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line, and it is true: six keys join a published catalog, nothing is removed or refused. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: the catalog is platform text, no schema key, accepted value or metadata type changes, and these doors consult no `errors.` override.

The claim on the card (7197524494) declared the first line as `no`. The PR's `yes (widening)` is the one the diff supports; the claim line is the seat's to reconcile.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag 1, a plural pair chosen by a bridge flag instead of a noun change: accepted.** The noun was already plural and the verb sits in the shared sentence, so the card's suggested edit could not produce "are". The outcome the card asks for (the sentence, the pins, the changeset line) is delivered.
- **Dev flag 2, whole sentences for the comment and redelivery doors: accepted.** Their English differs in wording from the bridge template, so only whole sentences keep it byte-identical, which the card requires.
- **Dev flag 3, the "no noun key stays English" control test removed: accepted.** It pinned an arm that no longer exists; the type now carries the requirement, and `TypeScript Type Check` is green on the three bridges.
- No `open_questions` entry: the claim is `mode:thread`, with no dev report on the card.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- **`Fixes #37610` is whole, not partial.** Item 1 (both doors from the catalog, four locales, English identical), item 2 (`nounKey` required) and item 3 ("are", pins, changeset line) are each delivered.
- Out-of-diff note for the seat, not a finding on this head: `packages/runtime/src/domains/approvals.ts` (`/approvals/act`) and `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts` (inbound hooks) answer the same two-sentence missing-service `501` as fixed English literals. The card names neither.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts`** holds against the card and against its consumers. The `_plural` pair follows the catalog's own stated rule (split the sentence, never the code), as `_required`, `_opaque` and `_untitled` do. I tried to break it five ways and none held: a locale missing a key (the every-locale test refuses it, and all four carry all six); a placeholder the caller does not fill (sets match per pair); noun and sentence resolved in different locales (both render from one caller object); a header-derived tag reaching a prototype member of the catalog (the resolver takes own keys only, and a miss falls to `en`); a consumer matching the old English text (none in the tree outside the pins).

**`own-door-bridge.ts`, `comments.ts`, `webhooks.ts`, `attachments.ts`** agree with the catalog sentence by sentence: the bridge reads the `_plural` pair only when `nounPlural` is set, only `ATTACHMENTS_BRIDGE` sets it, and the two handlers render their keys with the bridge's own locale reader and no params.

- N1 (nit) — `own-door-bridge.ts`: the header section title still reads "when the bridge names its noun". With `nounKey` required the condition is always true.
- N2 (nit) — `operation-message.ts`: the paragraph for `comment_doors_*` and `webhook_redeliver_*` does not say, as the `print_*` and `own_door_*` paragraphs do, that the locale is the request's top `Accept-Language` tag and that no `errors.` override is consulted. The handlers' own comments say it; the catalog omits it.
- N3 (nit) — `own-door-bridge.ts`: nothing ties `nounPlural` to the noun's number, or `nounKey` to a key the catalog holds, for a bridge added later. A plural noun without the flag would read "doors is" again, and a mistyped key would print the key itself. The pins name the three shipped bridges by hand.

All three sit in non-prose files, so a fix would move this head. They are accepted deviations here, or one follow-up card.
